subsystems.name: Vision backbone
subsystems.role: turns camera images into features the policy can reason over.
parts: image encoder (often a pretrained vision transformer)
tokeniser that splits frames into patches

subsystems.name: Language encoder
subsystems.role: makes a spoken or typed instruction a usable conditioning signal.

subsystems.name: Policy transformer
subsystems.role: maps fused vision and language features to a sequence of motor commands.
parts: action-chunking module that predicts several steps at once

subsystems.name: Action representation
subsystems.role: decides the output format — joint angles, end-effector poses, or discrete action tokens.

subsystems.name: Data pipeline
subsystems.role: collects, cleans and labels the demonstrations the model learns from.

subsystems.name: Runtime
subsystems.role: runs inference fast enough to control real hardware.
parts: real-time scheduler feeding the motor controllers

subsystems.name: Safety layer
subsystems.role: stops a wrong action before it damages anything.

buildSteps.title: Build a demonstration rig
buildSteps.detail: Cameras, joint encoders and a teleoperation interface so a person can drive the robot while every image, command and motion is recorded.

buildSteps.title: Collect a large, varied dataset
buildSteps.detail: Hundreds to thousands of episodes per task, across rooms, lighting, object positions and robot types, so the policy does not just memorise one setup.

buildSteps.title: Annotate with language
buildSteps.detail: Each episode or segment gets a plain instruction, which is what lets one model follow new phrasings instead of a fixed button.

buildSteps.title: Start from a pretrained vision-language model
buildSteps.detail: Reuse a model already trained on internet images and text, so the robot does not have to learn what a cup or a drawer looks like from scratch.

buildSteps.title: Fine-tune on robot actions
buildSteps.detail: Co-train the network to emit actions, keeping some vision-language data in the mix so the model does not forget general concepts.

buildSteps.title: Add preference or reward learning
buildSteps.detail: Human judgements of which attempt was better, or a learned reward model, refine behaviour beyond simply copying the demonstrations.

buildSteps.title: Evaluate in simulation, then on hardware
buildSteps.detail: Test many randomised scenes in simulation, then run closed-loop trials on the real robot and log every failure mode.

buildSteps.title: Deploy with action chunking and guardrails
buildSteps.detail: Run the model at the robot's control rate, predicting short bursts of motion, with hard limits that override the network.

buildSteps.title: Keep learning from deployment
buildSteps.detail: Successful and failed runs are fed back into the dataset, and the model is retrained on a regular cycle.

prerequisites.why: they supply the general scene and instruction understanding the policy builds on.
cross-robot datasets such as Open X-Embodiment exist, but they are small and uneven next to text or image corpora.
a learned policy is only as good as the actuators and controllers executing its commands.

prerequisites.tech: Cheap onboard compute for transformer inference
prerequisites.why: the model must respond in tens of milliseconds, which constrains size and precision.
without shared tests and accepted limits, results are hard to compare and hard to trust near people.

pathway.milestone: single-arm vision-language-action models doing tabletop tasks after fine-tuning
pathway.unlocks: one network handling many tasks instead of one program per task.

pathway.milestone: cross-robot generalist policies and whole-body control on humanoids
pathway.unlocks: rapid transfer to new hardware, so a new robot does not start from zero.

pathway.milestone: on-robot learning from its own experience with human feedback
pathway.unlocks: steady improvement in unstructured places such as homes and warehouses.

pathway.milestone: long-horizon reliability over hours with certified safety limits
pathway.unlocks: general-purpose labour, doing multi-step jobs unattended.
